claims.text: As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
Refractory high-entropy alloys can possess useful mechanical properties at room and elevated temperatures.
Atomic layer deposition can produce a conformal, ultrathin Al₂O₃ coating on as-cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The deposited Al₂O₃ layer will be uniformly adherent and pinhole-free.
The ALD Al₂O₃ layer will act as an oxygen-diffusion barrier at approximately 1000 °C.
The Al₂O₃ barrier will retard oxygen ingress into HfNbTaTiZr.
Retarding oxygen ingress will prevent or reduce detrimental oxide-scale formation.
The surface coating will not alter the alloy's bulk microstructure.
After 100 hours at 1000 °C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere, coated samples will have significantly less surface oxidation and oxide-scale growth than uncoated controls.
The coated alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility in the 8–16% range after the specified high-temperature exposure.
The coated alloy will retain a high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa under strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹ after the specified exposure.
The coating's protective effect will persist for exposures up to approximately 100 hours at 1000 °C in oxygen-rich environments.
Longer exposures or higher temperatures may compromise coating integrity and mechanical performance.
Thermal cycling, fluctuating oxygen partial pressure, or coating microcracking may reduce protection by permitting localized oxygen ingress.
